subject: Trading
title: Regulation After Crashes
description: A quick win: understand Regulation After Crashes.

hook.text: Every major crash produces major regulation. 1929 gave us the SEC. 2008 gave us Dodd-Frank. Crisis drives change.

buildup.text: Regulators react to crashes by identifying what failed and creating rules to prevent a repeat.

discovery.text: The SEC, FDIC, Glass-Steagall, Sarbanes-Oxley, Dodd-Frank—all were born from the ashes of financial disasters.

twist.text: Regulation fights the last war. The next crisis nearly always comes from a place regulators aren't watching.

climax.text: The cycle repeats: crisis, regulation, complacency, deregulation, innovation, new crisis. History rhymes.

punchline.text: We regulate after we crash—never before.

quiz.question: Which regulatory body was created after the 1929 crash?
